source_title: Remembering ‘Star Trek’ Actors Who Have Died — from Patrick Stewart to Walter Koenig - People.com
source_excerpt:
The beloved franchise debuted in 1966 with ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ which featured several actors who have since died
CBS Photo Archive/Getty; CBS via Getty; CBS via Getty
Star Trek first came to screens in 1966 with the premiere of Star Trek: The Original Series
The franchise has spawned several TV shows, movies and books since then
Several of its stars — including Patrick Stewart and Walter Koenig — have died over the years
Star Trek ’s 60-year legacy includes dozens of actors, including the late Sir Patrick Stewart .
The beloved science fiction franchise made its debut with the 1966 premiere of the Star Trek TV show, which was later renamed Star Trek: The Original Series . The show follows a series of crew members aboard the USS Enterprise as they explore the great unknown of outer space.
Since then, Star Trek has expanded with more TV shows, movies, video games and books — ultimately becoming one of the highest-grossing franchises of all time.
In the six decades since the launch of the franchise, several beloved cast members have died. Stewart, who introduced the world to his iconic character Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation , died on Oct. 28, 2026. His death followed that of Walter Koenig , who died three days prior and who was known for playing Ensign Pavel Chekov on Star Trek: The Original Series.
Here are 11 Star Trek actors who have died in the years since the franchise’s debut.
Koenig was one of the original cast members on Star Trek: The Original Series . The actor played Pavel from 1967 to 1969 and reprised his role in seven Star Trek movies.
Koenig, who was also a screenwriter, died on Oct. 25, 2026. He was 90.
“Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in Star Trek: The Original Series , Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit,” a rep for the actor told PEOPLE in a statement. “Beyond Star Trek , his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft.”
Although Stewart didn’t appear in the original Star Trek series, he quickly became a staple of the franchise.
Stewart began playing Jean-Luc on Star Trek: The Next Generation in 1987. He acted in all seven seasons of The Next Generation before reprising his role in four Star Trek films from 1994 to 2002 and the 2020 Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard .
Stewart’s longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, announced his death on Oct. 29, 2026. He was 86.
“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny , following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” Novak said in a statement shared with PEOPLE.
Novak continued,“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
Another beloved actor on Star Trek: The Original Series was Nichelle Nichols , who played Lt. Nyota Uhura. When the show premiered in 1966, Nichols made history as one of the first Black women to play a major role on a primetime TV show.
Nichols went on to star in six Star Trek movies with her original cast members, as well as two additional movies and five TV shows.
On July 30, 2022, Nichols died in Silver City, N.M. She was 89.
“Last night, my mother, Nichelle Nichols, succumbed to natural causes and passed away,” Nichols’ son, Kyle Johnson, wrote in a statement on her Facebook page . “Her light however, like the ancient galaxies now being seen for the first time, will remain for us and future generations to enjoy, learn from, and draw inspiration. Hers was a life well lived and as such a model for us all.”
Leonard Nimoy became one of the most recognizable stars on Star Trek: The Original Series with his role as the iconic half-Vulcan, half-human character Mr. Spock.
Nimoy also appeared alongside his original cast in six films, as well as Star Trek: The Next Generation and Star Trek Into Darkness .
Five years after he announced that he was officially retiring as Spock in 2010, Nimoy died on Feb. 27, 2015. He was 83.
The actor “passed away this morning after a long battle with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at his home in Bel Air,” his rep confirmed in a statement to PEOPLE at the time.
James Doohan portrayed beloved engineer Montgomery “Scotty” Scott in Star Trek: The Original Series , as well as in eight movies and a handful of TV shows.
Doohan’s final on-screen appearance as Scotty took place in the 1994 film Star Trek Generations . He died on July 20, 2005, after being diagnosed with pneumonia and Alzheimer’s disease, according to the Los Angeles Times . He was 85.
DeForest Kelley, who became known for his role as Dr. Leonard “Bones” McCoy on Star Trek: The Original Series , was the first member of the original TV show to die.
The actor appeared in seven Star Trek films and two additional TV shows. He died on June 11, 1999, at age 79, per Variety .
Grace Lee Whitney joined Star Trek: The Original Series during its first season as Janice Rand, the personal assistant to James T. Kirk ( William Shatner ).
Although Whitney only portrayed the character for eight episodes in season 1, she eventually reprised her role in seven other projects within the franchise.
On May 1, 2015, Whitney died at her home in Coarsegold, Calif., according to The Washington Post . She was 85.
Majel Barrett had a unique role in the Star Trek franchise, appearing as several different characters throughout her decades-long acting career.
Barrett, who was married to Star Trek creator Gene Roddenberry , appeared as Nurse Christine Chapel in Star Trek: The Original Series and two films, as well as Number One in The Original Series and Lwaxana Troi in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Star Trek: Deep Space Nine .
On Dec. 18, 2008, Barrett died at her home in Bel Air, Calif., after being diagnosed with leukemia, Reuters reported at the time. She was 76.
René Marie Auberjonois joined the Star Trek universe in 1993 when he began portraying shape-shifting character Odo on Star Trek: Deep Space Nine .
In addition to appearing in all seven seasons of Deep Space Nine , Auberjonois also briefly appeared in Star Trek: Enterprise as a character named Ezral in 2002.
Auberjonois was diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer in 2018 and died on Dec. 8, 2019, at his home in Los Angeles, Calif., per The New York Times . He was 79.
Aron Eisenberg became known for his recurring role as the Ferengi character Nog throughout all seven seasons of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine . He also made brief appearances in other Star Trek series and hosted a Star Trek podcast.
On Sept. 21, 2019, the actor died at age 50.
“He was an intelligent, humble, funny, emphatic soul,” Eisenberg’s wife, Malíssa Longo, wrote on Facebook at the time, per CNN . “There will never be another light like Aron’s. The beauty that he was and the legacy he leaves behind is beyond words.”
Anton Yelchin is one of the youngest members in the Star Trek universe to have died.
The actor made his Star Trek debut when he portrayed Pavel Chekov in the 2009 film Star Trek and reprised his role as Pavel in Star Trek Into Darkness and Star Trek Beyond .
Yelchin was 27 when he tragically died in a “fatal traffic collision” on June 19, 2016, his rep told PEOPLE at the time.
Prior to his death, Yelchin spoke to PEOPLE about playing Pavel, who was famously first portrayed by Koenig.
“[Koenig] came on set after I had, thankfully, finished most of my scenes,” Yelchin recalled in 2009. “Walter said, ‘Don’t let this become your life.’ That’s perfectly understandable. With me it’s always a desire to work with different characters. This is just another character. It happens to be an iconic role .”
